title: Streaming loss detection and reconciliation protocol for SSE-based responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers see partial or duplicated outputs when clients reconnect to long-lived SSE streams (chat/generation + function calls + structured JSONL). Root causes include transient dropped TCP segments, client-side stream reestablish without server-side gap info, and ambiguity around chunk boundary semantics for tool/function-call frames and structured output envelopes.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight reconnection handshake and fragment-reconciliation protocol that: (1) allows safe resume with minimal payload duplication, (2) preserves function-call/JSON structured boundaries across reconnects, (3) is compatible with existing fetch/Readablestream and SSE clients with graceful fallback, and (4) is simple enough to roll out behind a feature flag.

Design highlights:
- Fragment model: every emitted token chunk is annotated server-side with three stable attributes: sequence_anchor (monotonic integer per session), frag_type (data | meta | fn_start | fn_end | structured_envelope), frag_checksum (SHA1 hex of chunk payload). These are encoded in an SSE event-metadata envelope separate from the user-facing text to avoid polluting client parsers.
- Resume token: on disconnect, the client supplies the last-seen sequence_anchor and associated frag_checksum via an extension header ("x-rwd-resume-after: <anchor>:<checksum>") or as the first SSE comment after reconnection for fetch-based clients. Server validates checksum to detect partial-chunk replay vs full delivery.
- Reconciliation window: server accepts resume anchors up to N=256 anchors back. If anchor within window and checksum matches prefix semantics, server will stream only the missing anchors and then continue normal progression. If checksum mismatch (indicating server-side divergence or non-idempotent toolcall), server chooses safe fallback: issue a special SSE control event "rwd-resync" containing a snapshot_id and a single inline reconciliation marker that forces client to treat the next chunk as authoritative (leading to client-side dedup logic).
- Function/toolcall preservation: fn_start and fn_end frag_types act as atomic markers. The resume policy guarantees that a reconnect never returns a partial fn_* pair. If reconnect would land inside a functioncall pair, server opts to either (a) replay complete fn_start..fn_end if available in window, or (b) abort current function invocation and emit a control "rwd-fn-abort" with a machine-readable reason. Clients must prefer idempotent function handlers or implement dedup by function-call-id carried in meta.
- Structured output: structured_envelope fragments contain a compact JSONL header (schema_version, record_id, partial_flag) plus payload. Clients are expected to reassemble JSONL records using record_id; server ensures record_id uniqueness per session so reconnection can discard duplicates deterministically.
- Backpressure and ordering: sequence_anchor is authoritative ordering. We keep per-connection monotonic sequence generation and persist minimal lineage for N anchors to allow peer negotiation across short reconnections.
- Backoff and negotiation: support optional header "x-rwd-resume-protocol: v1" to opt into the handshake. Default behavior (header absent) remains existing streaming semantics (best effort reconnect with possible duplicates) to preserve backwards compatibility.

Success criteria / metrics:
- Reduce duplicate-token customer complaints by 80% on reconnection paths (measured via error telemetry and support tickets).
- No measurable >1% p99 additional latency for typical 1s token bursts in fast paths.
- Integration tests that simulate packet loss, client reconnects, and mixed functioncall/structured outputs pass deterministically.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Storing lineage for all sessions is expensive; we limit to rolling window (N=256) and persist it in-memory on serving nodes + replicated to nearest hot standby for quick failover. This increases memory footprint per session but avoids a central hot store read on every reconnect.
- Checksum validation is best-effort: for very long fragments we use prefix checksum to detect partial truncation vs full duplication (see implementation notes).
- Non-idempotent server-side toolcalls may still require higher-level application semantics; we will emit explicit abort markers for those cases and document recommended client handling.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike and reference client library changes (JS + Python) to support x-rwd-resume-after header and first-event comment resume handshake. (Spike PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/3121)
2) Implement server-side fragment envelope and windowed lineage store behind feature flag "stream-resume-v1". Add integration tests in CI simulating reconnects.
3) Add control events and client dedup helpers in SDKs.
4) Gradual rollout: internal alpha -> opt-in beta -> default on for hosted API within 8 weeks.

Risks: increased memory usage, potential for subtle client compatibility issues with older fetch polyfills (we will publish a compatibility note), complexity around functioncall atomicity for long-running tool ops.

comments: 2025-02-10 Triage: Identified as high-impact after multiple customer reports for reconnect duplication on hosted API. Assigned to Jonah.

2025-02-12 Spike complete: ran simulated reconnects with sequence_anchor windowing. Found memory vs window-size sweet spot at 256 anchors for typical session churn. Spike notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-stream-resume-spike
2025-02-18 Design review: PM (Mateo Ruiz) approved approach; Design (Lina Gomez) requested UX-considerate control event names and explicit user-doc copy for functioncall abort cases.
2025-02-22 Engineering: implemented fragment envelope encoder and checksum function. Initial tests pass locally. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/tree/stream-resume-v1

2025-02-27 Integration tests: added reconnect scenarios (TCP drop, client disconnect after partial chunk). Observed one flaky test where checksum prefix mismatch caused double-abort; adding stronger logging and a mitigation in reconcile path.
2025-03-03 SDKs: JS client PR open to honor resume header and to dedupe by sequence_anchor+record_id. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/456

2025-03-05 Code review: Runtime team requested clearer invariants around fn_start/fn_end handling and an explicit metric for 'forced-abort' events before merging. Working on follow-up PR with metrics instrumented.
